newsitem.title: USA: Florida judge sees "mother of all RICO actions".
newsitem.headline: Florida judge sees "mother of all RICO actions".

text.p: The judge who allowed Florida to apply anti-racketeering statutes in its lawsuit against the tobacco industry said on Friday that the case could be the "mother of all RICO actions."

"In its third amended complaint, the state alleges a parade of horribles that would seem to make out a case for the 'mother of all RICO actions,'" Palm Beach County Circuit Judge Harold Cohen wrote in his order allowing the state to proceed with claims under Florida's Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act.

"The extraordinary and grievous damages and injuries alleged to have flowed from defendants' alleged enterprises and alleged patterns of racketeering activity are the type for which the legislature intended the Florida RICO act to be applied," he said.

Florida Attorney General Bob Butterworth has said a victory against tobacco under the RICO act would allow the court to triple the more than $1.0 billion Florida has claimed. The suit seeks compensation from the tobacco industry for state expenditures to treat tobacco-related illnesses.
In the ruling Friday, Cohen said: "What is alleged is so far reaching and all encompassing that if liability is proven, application of RICO civil relief and recover would undoubtedly be warranted."
But the judge also warned that there was a big difference between allegations and proof of wrongdoing under a RICO statute.
"The court reminds all parties that allegations made and clear and convincing proof are two different things," Cohen wrote.
Cohen denied the motion by Philip Morris Cos and other tobacco companies to block the claims under RICO, saying that there was ample time and legal representation to prepare for the court date.
"The number of lawyers working on this one case for the defense (and for the state) is mind-boggling," he said.
Cohen said the court would permit no further amendments to the complaint.

"It is ordered and adjudged that the trial of this case shall proceed on the third amended complaint as set forth in this order beginning August 4, 1997, subject to motions for summary judgment to be heard by the court during the week of June 30, 1997, or any earlier date agreed to by the parties," Cohen said.
